comments.text:
Landed in `e3e81589`, merged as `9e5a4e5b`. `Makefile:15` is now
`GO ?= $(shell mise which go 2>/dev/null || echo go)`.

Evidence, in the order the acceptance criteria ask for it. Environment: `GOROOT` exported to
the version-manager install, `/usr/bin/go` reporting `go1.26.6-X:nodwarf5`, the version
manager reporting `go1.26.6`.

**The guard is capable of failing.** Bare `go build` on the same tree, same hostile `PATH`:

```
$ PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH go build ./cmd/ntm
# internal/profilerecord
compile: version "go1.26.6" does not match go tool version "go1.26.6-X:nodwarf5"
# unicode
compile: version "go1.26.6" does not match go tool version "go1.26.6-X:nodwarf5"
# internal/godebugs
```

**AC 3 — the same PATH through make now succeeds:**

```
$ PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH make build
/home/gabriel/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.6/bin/go build -trimpath -ldflags "..." -o ntm ./cmd/ntm
```

**AC 4 — the version stamp survives:**

```
$ ./ntm --version
ntm version v1.26.0-62-g0e3cff89-dirty
```

(`-dirty` is the uncommitted Makefile at the time of the run, not a defect.)

**AC 2 — an explicit override still wins,** proven by it failing, which is the only way to know
the value was actually used rather than ignored:

```
$ make build GO=/usr/bin/go
/usr/bin/go build -trimpath -ldflags "..."
# internal/goarch
```

**AC 1 — the fallback,** with a `PATH` carrying neither the version manager nor its shims
(`mise` lives at `/usr/bin/mise`, so excluding `/usr/bin` was not enough — a directory of
symlinks to `make`, `sh`, `git`, `date` and `go` was used instead):

```
$ env PATH=<no-mise-dir> make -n build
go build -trimpath -ldflags "..."
```

Correction carried into the description: the mechanism is a crossed `GOROOT`, not a rejected
build cache. The exported `GOROOT` is honoured by whichever driver `PATH` supplies, so a
mismatched driver invokes the other toolchain's `compile`. That is why pinning the driver is
the fix and why leaving `GOROOT` alone is correct.

title: Give the last fixed tmux session name a per-run suffix
description:
## Outcome

No test in the tree creates a tmux session under a name a person could plausibly be using.
`internal/robot/send_test.go` gets the same per-run unique suffix every other tmux-creating
test in the repo already carries, and a sweep confirms it was the last one without.

## Context

`internal/robot/send_test.go:155` assigns the bare literal `session := "ntm-send-render"`,
creates it at `:156`, and kills it from `t.Cleanup` at `:159-160`. It is the only unsuffixed
tmux session name found in the tree. Every other real-tmux test suffixes: `internal/robot/`'s
own `robot_test.go` uses `"ntm_test_bundle_privacy_" + time.Now().Format("150405")`,
`internal/tmux/session_real_test.go:23-25` has `uniqueSessionName`, and
`internal/pipeline/real_tmux_integration_test.go:378` and
`internal/tui/dashboard/real_tmux_integration_test.go:29` both append `UnixNano`.

Under working isolation this is harmless: the package's `TestMain`
(`internal/robot/robot_test.go:152-175`) sets an isolated `TMUX_TMPDIR`, so the name lives on
a private server where nothing else can hold it. It matters in exactly two situations —
when isolation is defeated, and when two runs of this package share one server, where the
second `CreateSession` collides on the name and the first run's cleanup kills the second
run's session.

This is deliberately a separate, smaller bead from the isolation-bypass one. The bypass is the
defect; this is the one place in the tree where that defect has a name to land on. Fixing
either without the other still leaves a real improvement, so they are not sequenced.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
tmux new-session -d -s ntm-send-render
NTM_TEST_TMUX_ENV_OWNED=1 go test ./internal/robot/ -run TestRobotSendVerifyRenderRealTmux
tmux has-session -t ntm-send-render   # exits non-zero: the pre-existing session is gone
```

The same collision happens without the environment variable when two runs of this package
share a tmux server.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The session name at `internal/robot/send_test.go:155` carries a per-run unique suffix,
      using the convention already in `internal/robot/robot_test.go`
      (`time.Now().Format("150405")`) rather than a third spelling.
- [ ] A sweep over every `tmux.CreateSession` call in `internal/`, `e2e/` and `tests/` finds no
      remaining session name that is a bare string literal. The sweep command and its output go
      in the closing comment, so the claim is checkable without re-running it.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/robot/ -run TestRobotSendVerifyRenderRealTmux` is green.
- [ ] Done when: the reproduction above leaves the pre-existing `ntm-send-render` session
      alive.

## Tests

- **Integration** (real tmux), existing: `TestRobotSendVerifyRenderRealTmux` passes with the
  renamed session, unchanged in every other respect.
- **Integration**, new: the same test run twice concurrently against one server does not have
  either run's cleanup kill the other's session.

## Blast radius

One assignment in `internal/robot/send_test.go`, plus whatever the literal-name sweep turns up
— expected to be nothing, and the bead is done either way once the sweep is recorded. No
production code.

title: Six internal/cli tests fail: fake agent panes are refused by the PANE_AGENT_DEAD guard
description:
## Outcome

`go test ./internal/cli/` passes on `main` with a live tmux. The six tests whose fake agents are
refused by the `PANE_AGENT_DEAD` guard either keep a foreground process the guard recognises, or
stop pretending to be agent panes — and the guard keeps refusing delivery to a pane whose agent
CLI really has exited, which is the defect it was added for.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On `main`, with a working `tmux` binary, run `go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1` (no `-short` —
   every one of these tests skips under `-short`).
2. Six tests fail, each with a message of this shape:

```
PANE_AGENT_DEAD: pane 1.3 is titled ...__cod_1_test-model but its foreground
process is "zsh" (agent CLI exited to a bare shell); restart it with
--robot-restart-pane, or target the user pane for deliberate shell input
```

Observed 2026-08-24 at `main`. Proven pre-existing rather than introduced by recent work: the
same six were run against `main` and against an older commit, each extracted with `git archive`
into a separate directory, and they fail identically in both.

## Context

**The six, and the three different fixtures behind them** — this is not one fixture with one bug:

- `testAgentCatCommandTemplate` (`internal/cli/testmain_test.go:12-15`) backs
  `TestAgentLifecycleSpawnWorkKill` (`internal/cli/lifecycle_test.go:18`),
  `TestRunReassignment_ToPane_Success` (`internal/cli/assign_reassign_test.go:244`) and
  `TestRunRetryAssignments_PreservesPreviousFailReasonAndMetadata` (`:350`, sharing
  `setupReassignSession` at `:143`). With a model set it renders to
  `: 'test-model' >/dev/null && /bin/cat` — a two-command shell list, so the shell stays as the
  pane's foreground process, and `cat` exits on stdin EOF.
- `configureSessionTemplateFakeAgents` (`internal/cli/session_templates_e2e_test.go:435-440`)
  backs `TestSessionTemplateSpawn_Builtin` (`:21`) and
  `TestSessionTemplateSpawn_CustomUserTemplate` (`:129`). It renders
  `/bin/sh -c 'stty -echo; printf …; while IFS= read -r line; do … done'` — the interpreter itself
  is `sh`.
- `TestDirectAssignCLIReplayIsDurableAndBypassesChangedPreflight` (`internal/cli/assign_test.go`)
  shares nothing: it writes its own `#!/bin/sh` script, launches it with
  `tmux.DefaultClient.Run("new-window", …)` and hand-sets the title with
  `tmux.SetPaneTitle(paneID, session+"__cc_1")`.

**What the guard actually compares.** `Pane.AgentCLIDead()` (`internal/tmux/session.go:601`)
returns false immediately unless the pane's stored `Type` — derived from its NTM-format title — is
a real agent type; otherwise it lower-cases the pane's live `pane_current_command`, reduces it to
a basename, and tests it against the fixed set `bareShellCommands` = `{zsh, bash, sh, fish, dash,
ksh, tcsh}` (`internal/tmux/session.go:592-594`). The message is formatted by
`RefuseDeadAgentPane` (`internal/dispatch/dispatch.go:317-324`), reached from two call sites:
`TMUXDeliverer.Deliver` (`internal/dispatch/dispatch.go:330`) and the inline deliverer of
`newShellDispatchServiceWithGate` (`internal/cli/send.go:3812`), which is the path `assign`,
`reassign` and `retry` route prompts through.

So every fixture above is capable of presenting a bare shell as the pane's foreground process,
while the title says the pane holds an agent. That is exactly the shape the guard exists to
refuse — it is not misfiring, it is correctly describing fake agents that do not look like
agents.

**The guard is newer than the fixtures, and landed without them.** `PANE_AGENT_DEAD`,
`AgentCLIDead` and `RefuseDeadAgentPane` all arrived together in `6f23ca95` (2026-08-04,
"refuse delivery to agent panes whose CLI is a bare shell"). That commit touched
`internal/cli/send.go`, `internal/dispatch/dispatch.go`, `internal/robot/is_working.go` and
`internal/tmux/session.go` — **no test fixture**. `testAgentCatCommandTemplate` dates to March
2026 and `configureSessionTemplateFakeAgents` to July, so both predate it by months.

**Why this is worth fixing rather than tolerating.** The failures are quiet in the two places
people look and loud in the one place nobody has looked yet:

- They **skip under `-short`**. All six call `testutil.RequireTmuxThrottled` as their first
  statement (`tests/testutil/throttle.go:115-125`, which skips on `testing.Short()` at `:117-118`
  before checking tmux at all). The repo's own quick gate is `go test -short ./...`, so the
  standard local check never sees them.
- They **do run in CI**: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs tmux (`:241-247`, `:301-302`, `:326`)
  and runs `go test -v -race -timeout=15m … ./...` at `:258` with no `-short`.
- **CI has never run.** `gh api repos/<fork>/actions/runs` reports `total_count: 0` — Actions is
  disabled by default on a fork and was never enabled. So the red is latent: it appears the day
  Actions is switched on, or the day this goes upstream.

Meanwhile the immediate cost is local and real: an unscoped `go test ./internal/cli/` already
fails, so a genuine new regression arrives inside six failures that everyone has learned to scroll
past.

**Three repair surfaces exist and none is half-built.** Reported so the work does not start by
re-deriving them:

- Make each fixture hold a foreground process the guard does not read as a bare shell — `exec` the
  loop or `cat` in place of the interpreting shell, and keep stdin from reaching EOF. Touches the
  three fixtures.
- Teach the guard about test panes. There is no existing env-var or flag hook in
  `AgentCLIDead` or `RefuseDeadAgentPane` to extend, so this is new production code whose only
  caller is the test suite — which is the option to justify hardest, not the one to reach for.
- Change what the tests target or assert. None of the six mistargets a pane today; each drives the
  pane it spawned, so this means changing the identity the test claims, not fixing a selection
  bug.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1` with a live tmux passes on `main`, with none of the six
      tests skipped to get there
- [ ] Each of the six is fixed at its own fixture: `testAgentCatCommandTemplate`
      (`internal/cli/testmain_test.go:12-15`), `configureSessionTemplateFakeAgents`
      (`internal/cli/session_templates_e2e_test.go:435-440`) and the inline script in
      `TestDirectAssignCLIReplayIsDurableAndBypassesChangedPreflight` — a fix that repairs one
      fixture and marks the others skipped does not satisfy this
- [ ] `Pane.AgentCLIDead` (`internal/tmux/session.go:601`) and `bareShellCommands` (`:592-594`)
      still refuse a pane whose agent CLI has genuinely exited to a shell — asserted by a test
      that spawns a fake agent, lets it exit, and expects `PANE_AGENT_DEAD`
- [ ] The `PANE_AGENT_DEAD` text and both call sites (`internal/dispatch/dispatch.go:330`,
      `internal/cli/send.go:3812`) keep their current behaviour for real panes
- [ ] If the guard gains any test-only accommodation, it is named in the commit body with the
      reason, and it cannot be reached in a production run — a code path whose only caller is the
      suite is a decision, not a detail
- [ ] The six tests fail before the fix and pass after it, demonstrated by running them at the
      parent commit, not asserted
- [ ] No test is newly gated behind `-short` or behind a tmux check that it did not already carry
- [ ] Done when: an unscoped `go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1` on a machine with tmux reports no
      failures, and a fake agent that exits to a shell still produces `PANE_AGENT_DEAD`.

## Tests

The six existing tests are the test: they already assert the behaviour, and the work is making
them exercise it again rather than writing new coverage.

**One new unit test is owed**, in the convention of the existing dispatch tests: a pane whose
title says agent and whose foreground process is a bare shell must still be refused with
`PANE_AGENT_DEAD`. Without it, the fix has no guard against being "corrected" later by loosening
`bareShellCommands` — which would silently restore the delivery failure the guard was added for.

**Regression check, run rather than reasoned**: the six at the parent commit fail, and at the fix
commit pass, on the same machine in the same session.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the change is fixture shape plus one assertion.

## Blast radius

The three test fixtures — `internal/cli/testmain_test.go:12-15`,
`internal/cli/session_templates_e2e_test.go:435-440`, and the inline script inside
`TestDirectAssignCLIReplayIsDurableAndBypassesChangedPreflight` in `internal/cli/assign_test.go` —
plus one new dispatch test. `internal/tmux/session.go` (`:592-594`, `:601`) and
`internal/dispatch/dispatch.go` (`:317-330`) are **read, not changed**, unless the work
deliberately takes the second repair surface, in which case the criterion above governs it. No
production behaviour changes for a real agent pane, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is not touched:
whether Actions is enabled on the fork is a separate decision from whether the suite is green.

comments.author: operator-review
comments.text:
Attempt merged as 99179923 and REVERTED as da150367 the same session. It introduced a regression, and the reason it did is the finding that matters for whoever takes this next.

WHAT THE ATTEMPT DID: the three fixtures were changed to hand the pane a process that is not a shell - awk reading stdin in place of the `while read` loop - so the pane's foreground process stops being `sh` while the fake agent waits. That part works. Of the five tests failing with PANE_AGENT_DEAD, four passed afterwards.

WHY IT WAS REVERTED: a test that was green before the merge went red after it.

    --- FAIL: TestRunReassignment_TargetBusyWithoutForce
        assign_reassign_test.go:685: expected error code TARGET_BUSY, got "RESERVATION_REQUIRED"

Verified against the parent commit with git archive: the same test passes there. So it is a regression from this change, not a pre-existing failure.

THE FINDING, and it invalidates the one-fixture approach: testAgentCatCommandTemplate is shared by tests that need OPPOSITE pane states, and the composer markers are the thing that decides which they get.

- With `printf '❯\n›\n' && /bin/cat` the pane reads as a ready agent, the two reassign tests pass, and TestRunReassignment_TargetBusyWithoutForce fails - it needs the pane to look busy, and instead the flow walks past the busy check into reservation and returns RESERVATION_REQUIRED.
- With `exec /bin/cat` the pane has no markers, TargetBusyWithoutForce passes and TestSessionTemplateSpawn_CustomUserTemplate passes, and the two reassign tests fail with "expected success envelope".

Both were measured, one after the other, in the same worktree. There is no single value of that template that satisfies both groups, so the fix cannot be one template: the fixture has to be split so each test gets the pane state it is actually asserting about, while none of them presents a bare shell.

WHAT STILL STANDS from the attempt: the awk approach for configureSessionTemplateFakeAgents and for the inline script in TestDirectAssignCLIReplayIsDurableAndBypassesChangedPreflight is sound and cost nothing elsewhere. The reverted diff is recoverable from 99179923.

ALSO ESTABLISHED, and worth not re-deriving:
- The count is five, not six. Measured twice on a clean base.
- Three tests in this package fail only in a full-package run and pass in isolation - TestSessionTemplateSpawn_Builtin, TestAgentLifecycleSpawnWorkKill, TestAgentLifecycleMultipleAgents. Contention, not fixture-dead. Do not fold them in.
- TestDirectAssignCLIReplayIsDurableAndBypassesChangedPreflight stops failing for the PANE_AGENT_DEAD reason once its fixture is repaired, and then fails at PANE_BUSY for a different defect entirely. That is bd-htr, and this bead now depends on it: the "Done when" here asks for the whole package green, which bd-htr blocks.
- Toolchain: a /usr/bin/go tagged go1.26.6-X:nodwarf5 cannot reuse a cache built by a plain go1.26.6 and fails with "compile: version ... does not match go tool version", which reads like a defect in the code under test. Build with the toolchain the module pins.

title: Decide whether --robot-inspect-coordination and --robot-restore take a session scope
description:
## Outcome

It is settled whether `--robot-inspect-coordination` and `--robot-restore` belong in the column
of robot queries that honour `--session` or in the column that refuses it, and the reason is
written down. Without this answer the classification sweep has two flags it cannot place, and a
sweep with a hole is a sweep whose enumeration test lies.

## Context

The 2026-08-23 inventory divided all 154 registered `--robot-*` flags by session scope. Every
bucket was decided from the code except two, and both are genuinely ambiguous rather than merely
unread.

**`--robot-inspect-coordination` (`internal/cli/root.go:2679`)** is keyed by `AgentName` alone.
Agent names here are NATO-phonetic and generated per session, so two live sessions can hold an
agent with the same name. Today the query answers about whichever one it finds. A session scope
would disambiguate — but it may be that agent names are meant to be unique fleet-wide, in which
case the collision is the defect and a scope is the wrong fix for it.

**`--robot-restore` (`internal/cli/root.go:2598`)** is keyed by a save-file path (`SavedName`).
The saved file may itself name the session it came from, so `--session` could mean three
different things: restore into that session, refuse when the file disagrees with it, or nothing
at all.

The other six queries in the ambiguous bucket were resolved: `--robot-snapshot` is `bd-jlv68`,
and `--robot-status`, `--robot-dashboard` and `--robot-terse` are one bead of their own. These
two are what is left, and each is a decision rather than a filter.

## Options

- **A · Both honour `--session`.** What changes: `--robot-inspect-coordination` disambiguates a
  repeated agent name instead of answering about an arbitrary one, and `--robot-restore` gains a
  target session. Cost: `--robot-restore` needs a rule for the case where the flag and the save
  file disagree, and that rule is a new behaviour nobody has asked for yet.
- **B · Both refuse `--session`.** What changes: both join the 86 queries with no session
  dimension, and passing `--session` to either is an error with a hint. Cost: the agent-name
  collision stays, silently — an inspect that answers about the wrong agent looks exactly like
  one that answers about the right one.
- **C · `--robot-inspect-coordination` honours it, `--robot-restore` refuses it.** What changes:
  the collision is fixed where it is real, and restore keeps being addressed by the artefact it
  restores from rather than by a session. Cost: the two neighbours in the same bucket end up in
  different columns, so the classification table has to carry the reason.
- **D · Fix the agent-name collision instead, and both refuse.** What changes: agent names become
  unique fleet-wide, which removes the ambiguity at its source rather than filtering around it.
  Cost: a change to name generation, which touches spawn and every surface that displays a name —
  much larger than the sweep that raised the question.

## What decides it

Are NATO-phonetic agent names intended to be unique across the whole fleet, or only within one
session? If fleet-wide, the collision is a bug and the answer is B or D; if per-session, the name
alone is not an address and the answer is A or C. The generation site and whether it consults
existing sessions is what settles it.

For `--robot-restore`, the second question is whether a saved file records the session it came
from. If it does, `--session` is at best a redundant assertion and at worst a contradiction to
resolve; if it does not, a target session is a real missing input.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the two flags is assigned to exactly one column — honours `--session` or refuses it
      — and the assignment is recorded on this bead
- [ ] The reason is recorded with it, including which of the two questions above decided it
- [ ] Any follow-on work the answer implies exists as its own bead before this one is closed
- [ ] Done when: the classification sweep can place both flags without asking anyone.

## Recovery path

Nothing is built here, so nothing is undone. If the answer proves wrong once implemented, the
follow-on bead it produced is what gets reverted, and this bead is reopened with the reason.

title: Health reports a working pane unhealthy from a stale scrollback error
description:
## Outcome

`--robot-health=<session>` stops reporting a working pane as `unhealthy` because of an error
string left in its scrollback minutes ago. The health surface reaches the same verdict about a
recovered pane as the classifier the coordinator uses, so an orchestrator reading health is not
told to worry about a pane that is fine.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run an agent pane and let it emit a transient error line — `connection reset`, or a Go binary
   printing `panic:` — then let it recover and keep producing output.
2. Run `ntm --robot-health=<session>` while the pane is working.
3. The pane reports `"health": "unhealthy"` with reason `error detected: …`, for as long as the
   line stays inside the 50-line scan window.

Established by reading the code on 2026-08-24, in the review of `bd-j5cdo`.

## Context

`bd-j5cdo` fixed the robot `StateClassifier`: an error matching outside the live tail no longer
produces `error` while the pane is progressing. **`internal/robot/health.go` has its own,
third error detector that the fix does not reach.**

`checkErrors` (`internal/robot/health.go:623-690`) does its own capture —
`tmux.CapturePaneOutputContext(ctx, paneID, 50)` at `:633` — and a plain `strings.Contains` scan
against `healthErrorPatterns` (`:422-449`). There is no live-tail window and no progress gating.
`HasErrors` (`:655-657`) becomes `HealthUnhealthy` in `calculateHealthState` (`:751`, reason
`"error detected: "`), and that reaches `GetSessionHealth` (`:895`) and the
`--robot-health=SESSION` JSON envelope (`:949-955`).

The asymmetry is inside this one file and is worth stating plainly: **stall detection is guarded
and error detection is not.** `checkStallWithActivity` (`:569-616`) builds a real
`NewStateClassifier` (`:577-580`) and calls `Classify()` (`:583`), so it inherits the live-tail
and progress logic. `checkErrors` next door does none of that.

**What this costs, and what it does not.** Traced end to end on 2026-08-24, because an earlier
review assumed worse:

- The verdict is **display and alerting only**. Nothing restarts a pane because of it.
- `AutoRestartUnhealthyAgent` (`:2189-2224`) is the one function gated on `HealthUnhealthy` that
  would restart, through `RestartManager.TryRestart` (`:2222-2223`) — and it has **no production
  caller anywhere in the tree**. It is unreachable code, which is the `WS2: wire or delete`
  epic's business, not this bead's.
- `--robot-health-restart-stuck` does restart panes, but `ClassifyStuckPanes` (`:2285-2317`) gates
  on `IdleSinceSeconds` and consults `Health` only to *exclude* `blocked` and `rate_limited`; an
  `unhealthy` pane is treated exactly like a healthy one. So the stale error neither causes nor
  prevents that restart.
- The continuous restart loop in `internal/resilience/monitor.go` is a different system on a
  different package (`internal/health`), which does not import `internal/robot` at all.

So the harm is a false `unhealthy` in a JSON surface an orchestrator reads — not a destroyed
agent context. That is why this is P3 and separate from `bd-j5cdo`, whose blast radius explicitly
excluded the pattern tables.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An error pattern matching outside the live tail does not by itself produce
      `HealthUnhealthy` while the pane shows output growth between two captures
- [ ] The same pattern matching inside the live tail still produces `HealthUnhealthy` with today's
      reason text
- [ ] A pane with a stale error and no output growth still reports `unhealthy` — a genuinely stuck
      pane is not rescued by this change
- [ ] `checkErrors` (`internal/robot/health.go:623-690`) and `checkStallWithActivity` (`:569-616`)
      reach their verdicts through the same guard, or the code says why two answers are correct
- [ ] `healthErrorPatterns` (`:422-449`) is not edited: the strings are right, the placement rule
      is what is wrong
- [ ] No additional tmux capture per health check — `checkErrors` already captures 50 lines at
      `:633` and `checkStallWithActivity` already classifies; the guard reuses what is captured
- [ ] `--robot-health-restart-stuck` classification is unchanged: it gates on idle time, and this
      bead must not make an `unhealthy` verdict start or stop mattering there
- [ ] Done when: a fixture pane whose buffer holds `connection reset` forty lines back and whose
      tail is growing reports `healthy`, and the same buffer with the match in the tail reports
      `unhealthy`.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven with fixture scrollback strings, in the convention of
`internal/robot/health_test.go` (see `calculateHealthState` cases at `health_test.go:100-230`):

- error string in the live tail, pane progressing → `unhealthy`
- error string outside the live tail, pane progressing → **not** `unhealthy` (the defect)
- error string outside the live tail, no growth → `unhealthy` (the stuck pane)
- no error string anywhere → unchanged
- `panic:` and `connection reset` each covered, since they take different branches in
  `healthErrorPatterns`

**Regression test** that `ClassifyStuckPanes` (`:2285-2317`) treats the same fixtures exactly as
it does today, so a change to the health verdict does not silently change which panes are
restartable.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the change is where a pattern is allowed to match.

## Blast radius

`internal/robot/health.go` — `checkErrors` (`:623-690`) and, if the two are reconciled, its
relationship to `checkStallWithActivity` (`:569-616`). `healthErrorPatterns` (`:422-449`),
`calculateHealthState` (`:741-760`), the restart machinery (`:1678+`) and the stuck-pane
classifier (`:2285-2317`) are **read, not changed**. Nothing outside this file is touched, and no
other classifier is involved.
close_reason: Implemented in cfd84924. checkErrors now shares the StateClassifier with checkStallWithActivity and applies the same live-tail plus progress guard to healthErrorPatterns: a match outside the live tail is dropped while the pane is progressing or parked at a fresh idle prompt, and kept when it is stuck. healthErrorPatterns unchanged, no extra tmux capture, ClassifyStuckPanes untouched. Verified by mutation in both directions: removing the guard turns three recovered-pane cases red, and making it always drop turns the two stuck-pane cases red, so the fix cannot be loosened or tightened without a test failing. internal/robot green.

title: Give --robot-rano-stats a session filter
description:
## Outcome

`--robot-rano-stats` accepts `--session` and reports statistics for the panes of that session
only. It is the last robot query that answers about per-session state with no way to say which
session.

## Context

The 2026-08-23 inventory of the 154 registered `--robot-*` flags put eight queries in the bucket
"answers about per-session state, ignores `--session`". Seven of them already filter by a session
flag of their own and only need renaming — that is the convergence bead. **`--robot-rano-stats`
(`internal/cli/root.go:3063`) is the eighth, and the only one with no session filtering of any
kind.** Its only selector is `--panes`, and a pane identifier is not unique across sessions, so
even that selector cannot express "this session's panes" without the caller enumerating them
first.

`--session` is registered on the same flag set as every robot flag (`internal/cli/root.go:4787`),
so passing it here parses cleanly and is then discarded — the same silent-wrong-scope failure
measured on `--robot-status`, with the difference that here there is no filtering machinery to
route it into. This is why it is its own bead rather than a line in the convergence one: the work
is new filtering logic, not a rename.

The resolution path to reuse is the shared one — `resolveRobot…Session`
(`internal/cli/root.go:5387-5401`) falling back to `robotSharedSession` (`:4787`) — so the flag
plumbing is settled and what this bead owes is the filter underneath it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--robot-rano-stats --session <name>` reports statistics computed only from the panes of
      that session
- [ ] The session is resolved through the shared helper path (`internal/cli/root.go:5387-5401`),
      not through a resolution written for this query
- [ ] With no `--session`, the output is byte-identical to today's — asserted
- [ ] `--panes` and `--session` given together intersect: the named panes, restricted to that
      session, with a pane outside the session reported rather than silently dropped
- [ ] A `--session` naming a session that does not exist returns `success:false` with
      `error_code: SESSION_NOT_FOUND`
- [ ] The scoped answer differs from the unscoped answer whenever a second session has panes —
      the criterion that proves the filter runs
- [ ] Done when: with two live sessions holding panes, `ntm --robot-rano-stats --session <one>`
      counts only that session's panes.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven, over a stubbed pane inventory so no tmux server is needed, in the
style of `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go`:

- scoped to one of two stub sessions → only that session's panes counted
- unscoped → every pane, output unchanged from today (regression)
- `--panes` plus `--session`, all panes inside the session → the named panes
- `--panes` plus `--session`, one pane outside the session → that pane is reported, not dropped
- unknown session → `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the change is one filter over a list.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/root.go` — the `--robot-rano-stats` dispatch branch at `:3063` and the shared
resolution helpers at `:5387-5401` — plus the statistics function it calls in `internal/robot/`,
which gains a session scope. No other robot query, no classifier and no capture path is touched.

title: Print a readiness verdict per pane at spawn
description:
## Outcome

`ntm spawn` prints one readiness verdict per pane: which classifier decided the pane was ready
to receive its prompt, or that no classifier exists for that agent type and delivery was
allowed unchecked. A run where prompts silently do not arrive is visible in the spawn output
instead of being discovered forty turns later.

## Context

On 2026-08-22 a six-pane swarm lost roughly thirteen minutes and forty turns to prompts that
were never delivered. The post-run survey's own words were that a single line — *"this agent
type has no classifier, prompts were not delivered, send them yourself"* — would have saved the
whole manual-delivery detour. The proximate cause that day was a stale installed binary, but
the reason it cost an hour is that **nothing in the spawn output says whether readiness was
established, guessed, or skipped.**

The delivery gate is `ComposerReadyForDelivery` (`internal/tmux/session.go:2331`, public wrapper
at `:2359`). It resolves a per-type composer marker through `composerMarkerForAgent`
(`internal/tmux/session.go:2203`), and **that table defines exactly two entries** —
`AgentClaude` → `❯` and `AgentCodex` → `›`. For those two it falls back to
`agent.ClaudeActivelyWorking` / `codexLooksWorking`.

**For every other agent type the gate fails open, silently.** The comment at
`internal/tmux/session.go:2326-2328` states it outright: unknown agent types, empty captures and
capture errors all return `ready=true`. Failing open is a defensible default — a gate that
blocks delivery on an unrecognised pane would strand every new agent type — but it is currently
indistinguishable, from the outside, from a pane that was actually checked.

A second path is quieter still: `buildSpawnPromptSequenceForAgent`
(`internal/cli/spawn.go:3938`) returns an **empty step list** for a type whose delivery is not
implemented (`ValidateAutomatedPromptDelivery`, `internal/agent/types.go:181`, which today fails
closed only for Grok — `ErrAutomatedPromptDeliveryNotImplemented`, `internal/agent/types.go:38`
and `:46`). Nothing is printed and spawn exits 0. A pane that will never receive its prompt
looks exactly like a pane that did.

By contrast the **timeout** path is already loud: `waitForSpawnPaneReady`
(`internal/cli/spawn.go:5932`) leads to `"⚠ Warning: spawn prompt delivery failed for agent %d:
%v"` (`internal/cli/spawn.go:3300`), recorded through `recordSetupError` and aggregated after
`setupWg.Wait()` into `"spawn prompt setup failed: …; the session and affected panes still
exist"` (`internal/cli/spawn.go:3440-3443`), with a non-nil error out of `RunE`. So the machinery
for reporting per-pane setup outcomes exists — it just has nothing to say about the two silent
cases.

**What PR #3 already fixed, and what this bead is not.** Commit `d58a18eb` ("Qualify tmux session
targets, and make pi panes classifiable", 2026-08-21, 14 files, 623 insertions) added the `pi`
status-line prompt pattern and the `knownAgentTypes` entries for `pi` and `agy`
(`internal/status/patterns.go`), pi-specific detectors in `internal/agent/patterns.go`, the
wiring in `internal/status/unified.go`, and session-target qualification in
`internal/tmux/session.go` and `internal/resilience/monitor.go`. That fix is merged and the
installed binary now carries it. **This bead does not re-fix pi; it makes the verdict visible
for every type, including the ones nobody has written a classifier for yet.**

Note that the two classifiers are keyed the same way — `agent.AgentType.Canonical()`, which
normalises `claude`→`cc` and `codex`→`cod` — so the verdict line can name the canonical type
without inventing a second vocabulary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ntm spawn` prints exactly one readiness line per pane, naming the pane, the canonical
      agent type, and one of three verdicts: checked-and-ready, no-classifier (delivery allowed
      unchecked), or delivery-not-implemented
- [ ] The no-classifier verdict names what the operator must do — send the prompt by hand — and
      is printed for every type outside the `composerMarkerForAgent` table
      (`internal/tmux/session.go:2203`)
- [ ] A type whose prompt sequence comes back empty from
      `buildSpawnPromptSequenceForAgent` (`internal/cli/spawn.go:3938`) produces the
      delivery-not-implemented verdict rather than silence
- [ ] The existing timeout warning at `internal/cli/spawn.go:3300` and the aggregated error at
      `:3440-3443` keep their current text and their current non-zero exit
- [ ] The gate keeps failing open: no agent type that spawns today starts failing to spawn
      because of this change — the verdict is reporting, never enforcement
- [ ] The verdict lines survive `--robot`/JSON output as a field, not only as human text, so an
      orchestrator can read them
- [ ] Spawning six panes adds no more than one extra tmux capture per pane over today's spawn
- [ ] Done when: spawning a pane of a type with no composer marker prints the no-classifier
      verdict, and spawning `claude` and `codex` panes prints the checked verdict.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven in the convention of `internal/status/patterns_test.go`
(`TestIsPromptLine` at `:45`, `TestDetectIdleFromOutput` at `:99` — slices of
`{name, line, agentType, expected}` run through `t.Run`). Cases, one per verdict:

- `cc` and `cod` with a composer marker present → checked-and-ready
- a type absent from `composerMarkerForAgent` → no-classifier verdict, and `ready=true`
  unchanged
- an empty capture and a capture error → no-classifier verdict, `ready=true` (the fail-open
  contract, asserted rather than assumed)
- a type whose prompt sequence is empty → delivery-not-implemented verdict
- a readiness timeout → existing warning text, unchanged, and a non-nil error

Plus one **end-to-end** spawn test in the style of `internal/cli/spawn_error_test.go`, injecting
the existing `spawnSessionObserver` / `spawnPromptDispatcher` interfaces (the codebase has no
global fake tmux; those seams are how spawn is tested), asserting one verdict line per pane and
the exit status.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/spawn.go` — the per-agent block at `3260-3335` and the summary after
`setupWg.Wait()` at `3420-3460`, where per-pane setup outcomes are already assembled — plus a
verdict value returned from or alongside `ComposerReadyForDelivery`
(`internal/tmux/session.go:2331-2359`). `composerMarkerForAgent` and the fail-open behaviour are
**read, not changed**. No change to `internal/status/patterns.go` or to any classifier: this
bead reports what the existing ones decide.
